Bot Goal: Treat broad safety complaint as staff-review emergency until hazard is classified.
Tenant-Facing First Response: I’ll treat this as a safety concern first. Please keep away from the affected area and do not attempt a repair.
Required Intake Questions: What safety concern are you reporting? Location? Is anyone injured or in immediate danger? Is there gas smell, fire/smoke, electrical hazard, water, structural issue, lock/security problem, pest/wildlife, or alarm issue?
Safety Screening Questions: Any immediate danger, injury, gas/smoke/CO, sparks, active water near electrical, structural instability, blocked exit, or security exposure?
Safe Troubleshooting Allowed: No repair troubleshooting; safe distance, stop use, photos if safe.
Safe Troubleshooting Steps: Stay away from the hazard. Stop using affected equipment/area. Upload photos/video only if safe. Use emergency services guidance for life-safety situations per company script.
Troubleshooting Not Allowed: Do not tell the resident they are responsible for payment. Do not promise a vendor or timeline. Do not instruct the resident to open panels, handle wiring, climb roofs/ladders, bypass safety devices, disassemble equipment, repair gas/electrical/HVAC/roof/structural/major plumbing components, or keep resetting breakers.
Emergency Escalation Triggers: Any immediate danger, injury, fire/smoke/gas/CO, electrical hazard, flood/sewage, structural/falling hazard, or security exposure.
Urgent Escalation Triggers: Potential safety concern without immediate danger but not fully ruled out.
Routine Routing Rule: Do not route as routine until staff reclassifies.
Likely Vendor Category: Staff triage first; vendor depends on hazard type.
Dispatch Threshold: Immediate staff review; emergency escalation if life-safety trigger.
Photo/Video Conditions: Photos/video only if safe from distance.
Access Information Required: Ask for best phone number, preferred contact method, property access constraints, occupied/unoccupied status, and whether any rooms/areas are inaccessible.
Permission-to-Enter Questions: Ask: May maintenance enter if you are not home? Are there any restricted dates/times? Is there anything the vendor needs to know before entering?
Pet/Alarm/Gate Questions: Ask whether pets are present, how they will be secured, whether there is an alarm code, gate code, lockbox, parking note, or special entry instruction.
Possible Tenant-Caused Indicators: Unknown; possible misuse/tampering/impact only staff may evaluate.
Staff Review Required: Yes - always.
Houston/Texas Operational Notes: Houston-area operations: screen for active water, heat illness risk during summer AC outages, storm/wind damage, pest pressure, and HOA/exterior visibility issues. Use company emergency matrix; do not cite statutes to residents.
